title: George Foster's warning and the gold band in Memphis
summary: Foster warns Manetta about taking Desvigne over Sharper; Desvigne had to switch to a gold trumpet for the band and they rehearsed in Memphis.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Wouldn't tell me all he do, right here he lives, and I knock on the door. It was George Foster's wife came in. So he goes back in the kitchen and talks and tells me what. I told him all these fellas, it's funny actually. He said, well I'll tell you. Be careful, he says. So... You made a mistake of one thing that you done while they don't like you. By taking DejVe with you and leaving Bob Schauffer going to organize the band. You see? They say, watch these guys who's not allowed to do your thing. He said, alright. We players. We leave, take a trip up to St. Paul. Down for our way. Yeah, the boat. Alright. Come down. Now, on the following Sunday, we had to meet him in Memphis. Remember? Yeah. You come on the boat, you had a brand new horn, a silver, you had a CG clone, a silver horn. You had to change it and get a gold horn because the band was Allie's gold band.
That's right. The gold band. I had to get a gold trumpet.
Yeah, yeah. You had to change your head. That's right. That's right. I met you about two o'clock in Memphis on a Sunday evening. And, uh, we had a little rehearsal.
We had a little rehearsal, man.
Yeah. And that night, we, uh, we played. And I went out to town.
You remember that place? Yeah, yeah.
